comment: Repo-side freshness pins for every citation in signoff/block-manifest.json.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `klt signoff --manifest` compares a manifest's
`content_hash` against the *cited envelope's own* claim about its input --
it never opens the underlying artifact. klt 0.6.0 says so itself, on every
pinned citation: `input: not re-hashed (content_hash compared against this
envelope's own claim only -- the artifact itself was not read)`. Two
hand-written files agreeing with each other proves nothing, so this file
records the sha256 of the artifact each citation is really about, and
signoff/check.sh re-hashes it on disk in CI. That is what makes a citation
here fail rather than rot when its artifact moves.
As of issue #127 every citation in the manifest carries a manifest pin;
none is structurally unpinnable any more. Item 6 was the last holdout --
its Monte Carlo envelope was produced by klt 0.2.0
(layout/requirements.txt's *original* pin), which wrote
`provenance.input: null`, and a manifest `content_hash` against an
envelope that claims no input hash renders the item unmet/stale_evidence
-- a false negative. #127 re-pointed it at the campaign's current record
(`20260925-131502-808cece`), whose `provenance.input.content_hash` is
real, so the manifest pins it directly and this file's entry is now the
second, independent on-disk check rather than the only one.
Item 4's LVS citation no longer needs that workaround either (issue #127):
it was re-pointed at the current klt 0.6.0 record
(`20260924-221912-a947aa8`, the one `layout/ldo-core/reports/LATEST-LVS`
names) whose `provenance.input.content_hash` is
non-null, so the manifest now pins it directly. Its two entries below
stay anyway -- `environment.layout_sha256`/`environment.reference_sha256`
are a second, independent claim the manifest pin alone does not cover
(same discipline item 3's and item 7's entries below apply).
`envelope_field` is a dotted path into the cited envelope whose value must
equal `sha256`; null means the envelope makes no hash claim about this
artifact and only the on-disk re-hash is checked.

pins.note: The composed LDO-core GDS the `klt drc` run read. Also the manifest's own item-3 pin, so all three -- file on disk, envelope claim, manifest pin -- must agree.

Re-pinned by issue #127 against the klt 0.6.0 re-run's own copy of the composed LDO-core GDS (previously klt 0.2.0's 20260825-123628-3b4e121, whose lvs envelope carried no provenance.input at all). Specifically the *current* such record, 20260924-221912-a947aa8 -- the one layout/ldo-core/reports/LATEST-LVS names. The earlier klt 0.6.0 re-run 20260924-181216-50554fe (PR #155) would satisfy the provenance requirement identically, but it predates commit 0c65db2 (#163, VIN/VOUT sized as spec-derived power rails), which redrew the layout and produced this record; citing 50554fe would pin item 4 to a layout revision main has already superseded. The two lvs.json envelopes are byte-identical apart from the layout hash -- same status: match, same three warning-severity mismatches, same power_connectivity/body_verification blocks -- so this is a citation-currency fix, not a result change. This GDS is not byte-identical to item 3's still-3b4e121-vintage GDS -- item 3 was not in #127's scope -- so this hash is checked only against this envelope's own environment.layout_sha256 and, now, the manifest's own item-4 content_hash pin (provenance.input.content_hash == environment.layout_sha256 on this record, so both agree on one value).

The schematic-derived reference netlist the layout was compared against -- item 4 requires the compare to be against item 1's netlist, so the reference side needs pinning too, not just the layout side. Re-pinned by issue #127 alongside the GDS entry above; the manifest pin covers only the layout (input) side, not this reference side.

The netlist the Monte Carlo campaign ran on. Re-pointed by issue #127 from the klt 0.2.0 record 20260825-083111-4cb27f8, whose sim envelope wrote provenance.input: null and named the netlist only by an absolute path from the machine that produced it, so no manifest pin was possible and this on-disk hash was the citation's only freshness handle. The current record carries a real provenance.input.content_hash (identical to its own environment.netlist_sha256), so the manifest pins it directly and this entry cross-checks it on disk. WHICH record, and what changed with it: 4cb27f8 is twice superseded -- 20260925-110312-8280915 supersedes it and 20260925-131502-808cece supersedes that, per each record's own Supersedes field -- so 4cb27f8 was no longer the campaign of record for this block at all; measurements/characterization.md's Output row already cites 808cece. The intermediate 8280915 (status=error, 185 pass / 12 fail / 3 error of 200) would have kept item 6's klt-signoff reason at check_failed, but citing a record its own successor replaces, in order to keep a reason token steady, is not a freshness pin -- it is the opposite of one. 808cece is the campaign's current, correct result after issue #164 fixed the bench's initial-condition contract: status=pass, 200/200, vout_ss mean 1.80157 V inside the ratified 1.764-1.836 V window with a 3-sigma window of [1.776, 1.82714]. Item 6's verdict does NOT change -- it was unmet before and is unmet now, and t1_met_count stays 3 -- but its graded reason moves check_failed -> wrong_kind, because the cited check no longer fails on its own terms and item 6 asks specifically for a klt yield report, which does not exist for this campaign (docs/cli/signoff.md). That is a more accurate machine-readable statement of this block's position, not a weaker one: the statistical evidence is now a passing campaign with no yield report over it, where before it was a failing campaign measured on a bench with a known, since-fixed defect. Disclosed in full in signoff/README.md -> 'Item 6 cites the current campaign, and its reason changed with it'.
The `klt pex` run's input layout -- the same composed GDS items 3 and 4 were run on, which is what makes the (errored) post-layout leg comparable to them at all.
The extracted netlist the post-layout re-simulation was attempted against.

The aggregated per-spec-row rollup the generic envelope wraps. Regenerating it (measurements/build_characterization_report.py) without re-pinning here fails CI, which is the point: item 8 asks for a *current* artifact. Re-pinned by issue #142, by issue #154, and again by issue #118 (which re-ran the Output, Line regulation and Load regulation rows in full against the post-#116 DUT: all three rows' cited record ids change and all three flip STALE -> fresh, while all three verdicts stay FAIL -- the rollup is still 9 FAIL / 3 PASS / 4 N/A, so this envelope's own summary is unchanged). The two earlier re-pins -- both re-cut the DRC/LVS/PEX records the rollup's freshness table cites, and neither touched its 12 graded spec rows (still 9 FAIL / 3 PASS, as the envelope's summary says). #154's re-cut also flips the PEX detail line from status=pass to status=fail, which is the request declaring limits for the first time rather than a result getting worse -- see sim/pex-post-layout/README.md. Re-pinned again by issue #164, which changed sim/mc-output-accuracy's initial-condition contract (`tran ... uic`, EN as an edge) after measuring that the pre-#164 unconstrained `.op` handed 12 of 200 mismatch draws a start state that is not a circuit state (FB hundreds of volts ABOVE the VOUT node feeding it through a passive divider). The Output row's cited record becomes 20260925-131502-808cece and its verdict moves FAIL -> PASS, so this rollup is now 8 FAIL / 4 PASS / 4 N/A and the envelope's own summary is updated to match. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see design/README.md "#164". signoff/records/t1-tier-report.json carries the same new hash on its item-8 citation, edited in place rather than regenerated: `uvx --from klayout-tools==0.6.0` on the sweep host resolves to a git build (0.6.0+g983394050cff) whose grading_ruleset_id and item texts differ from the pinned release, so `check.sh --write` there would rewrite the yardstick instead of the evidence move. `content_hash` is the only field a faithful pinned regeneration changes. Re-pinned again by issue #180, which brought sim/load-transient into conformance with the same initial-condition contract (#171) #164 established: its `tran 200n 3m` now releases from an eleven-node `.ic`-constrained operating point instead of an unconstrained loop-closed `.op`, and the bench was re-run over the full 45-corner PVT matrix. The Load transient row's cited record becomes 20260926-013955-6449a98 and its Freshness flips STALE -> fresh, but its verdict stays FAIL, so this rollup is still 8 FAIL / 4 PASS / 4 N/A and the envelope's own summary needs no edit -- only `content_hash` moves. The row's own numbers did move: 0/45 corners PASS against the superseded record's 25/45, because that record predates #119 and measured neither the recovery-time clause (all 45 new failures) nor the 4.7uF C_out; the peak-excursion clause it did measure now passes at every corner. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "`load-transient` after #180". Re-pinned again by issue #179, which converted sim/loop-gain and sim/psrr-dc to the initial-condition contract's .nodeset-seeded .ac shape (#171) and re-ran both 45-corner matrices: the PSRR row's cited record becomes 20260926-033606-4a9ec09 and the Stability row's 20260926-040338-4a9ec09, and both rows flip STALE -> fresh (their predecessors predate #116/#139's pass-device resize). BOTH VERDICTS STAY FAIL, so this rollup is still 8 FAIL / 4 PASS / 4 N/A and this envelope's own summary is unchanged. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "#179". Re-pinned again by issue #189, which closed the two corners sim/thermal still had on the #171 solver-diagnostic gate after #178's seeding: one of the thirteen nodes in its `.nodeset` card (EA_TAIL, the error amplifier's PMOS input-pair source node) was written `'vsup'`-relative although three cold-start settles at ss/80C -- one per supply on the corner axis -- put its supply slope at 0.24 V/V, so the card sat 288 mV below the real node at vsup = 2.97 V. Correcting the classification (same measured number, absolute instead of `{vsup-0.836}`) takes the bench to 15/15 PASS with 0 of 15 corner logs carrying a diagnostic. The Thermal row's cited record becomes 20260926-095154-f6ab418 and its verdict moves FAIL -> PASS, so this rollup is now 7 FAIL / 5 PASS / 4 N/A and this envelope's own summary is updated to match. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "#189". signoff/records/t1-tier-report.json carries the same new hash on its item-8 citation, edited in place for the reason #164's note records above. Re-pinned again by issue #187, which corrected sim/dropout-vs-load's supply convention: that bench was the only one in sim/ driving EN off the VIN rail (VIN pinned at 3.63V for every corner while 'vsup' drove EN alone), which put EN 0.66V below VIN at the '*_2.97v' corners and, at fs/125C, left the VIN-sourced shutdown clamps M_ENP/M_ENP2 conducting 1.377uA/1.639uA against a 39pA/62pA leakage floor -- more than the error amplifier's whole 1.003uA tail current, so EA_OUT was pulled to VIN and the block never came up. EN now tracks VIN and the ramp's endpoint tracks 'vsup' so its rate stays the constant 266.3 V/s earlier records ran at. The Dropout row's cited record becomes 20260926-102849-0b63ae4 and stays fresh; its VERDICT STAYS FAIL (0/45, 0.32997-0.67307V against the 300mV bound, the largest per-corner change being 0.010mV), so this rollup is still 7 FAIL / 5 PASS / 4 N/A and this envelope's own summary needs no edit -- only `content_hash` moves. What did change is that the row's evidence no longer reports a failing vout_at_max_vin_v corner: the -7.4521V reading at fs_125c_2.97v was the bench convention, not the design. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "#187". Re-pinned again by issue #196, which fixed the LAST bench carrying the same EN-below-VIN geometry: sim/line-regulation drove EN at the corner runner's 'vsup' while its own VVIN was 'alter'ed 2.97-3.63V inside every corner, so the VIN=3.63V point of every *_2.97v corner ran with EN 0.66V below VIN. EN now tracks the instantaneous VIN. Unlike #187 this one does NOT move a record: #196 committed the corrected deck but could not hold the ~7h serial 45-corner re-run on the sweep host (measured: 578.9s for one corner against 41.7s in the cited record), so the Line regulation row still cites 20260926-001833-228fbc7 and its FRESHNESS FLIPS fresh -> STALE -- the row's verdict, its cited record id and the 7 FAIL / 5 PASS / 4 N/A rollup are all unchanged, and this envelope's summary needs no edit; only `content_hash` moves. The staleness is the honest state, the same one current-limit has carried since #177: see sim/README.md "#196" -> "Why the 45-corner matrix is not re-run here".
